To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human SP and whole semen (diluted up to 1/400) suppress the expression of natural and activated antitumour human cytotoxicity.
human seminal plasma (henceforth referred to as SP) suppresses natural cytotoxicity and the cytotoxicity induced by alpha-, beta- and gamma-interferon and interleukin-2.

1) human SP contains an activity that abrogates natural and interferon- or interleukin-2 activated human cytotoxicity; 2) this activity is not the result of lymphotoxic effects; 3) SP does not affect the expression of cytolytic effector function; and 4) the cytotoxic potential of SP treated human PBMC can be restored by further in vitro exposure to IFN or IL2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the components in seminal plasma that suppress the immune response and the elucidation of the mechanism(s) by which they suppress.
the study of the biological properties of human seminal plasma and its effects on the immune system.
the role of SP as a suppressor of human antitumorous immune function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SP is a suppressive agent in vitro.
human SP contains one or more substances that can suppress human antitumoral cytotoxicity.
SP and S are capable of suppressing the expression of natural and activated cytotoxicity in human PBMNC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytotoxicity against tumour cells of human PBMNC is markedly suppressed by SP and S, and that this suppression may be partially overcome by IFN and IL-2.
SP contains one or more factors which inhibit the expression of human natural killer activity.
the cytotoxicity and cytostatic activity of human mononuclear cells is inhibited by components present in SP and that this inhibition is partially reversible by interferon and IL2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SP contains components that can inhibit the expression of cytotoxic activity of human PBMNC against a variety of target cell lines.
SP is a potent inhibitor of human immune function.
SP can suppress immune functions, and that the suppression of immune function is not necessarily a good thing.
